items.text: Sky News Arabia reported that IRGC experts visited the port and airport of Al-Mokha and the Bab al-Mandab area. Iranian equipment has arrived in Houthi-controlled areas on Yemen's western coast. The Houthis have started installing radar on hills overlooking the Red Sea.

Hossein Abdollahi, the temporary Friday prayer leader of Dezful, said that a girl who stays late at cafes and shops will neither be a good child, a suitable mother, nor a successful spouse. He added that such a person only experiences momentary pleasures and is not inclined to planning or hard work.

The Israeli army announced that it has put its forces on full alert on all fronts during the Yom Kippur holiday. This measure is to counter potential threats. The news was reported by Ashkan Safaei, a journalist from Iran International.

Kim Jong-pyo, the South Korean ambassador to Iran, performed the song "Sultan of Hearts" on the 64th anniversary of diplomatic relations. The performance was with the Mitra Orchestra. The South Korean embassy described this as a musical gift to show respect and affection for Iran and its culture.
A father of a child told Iran International in a video that he paid over 1.2 million tomans for fever and pain-reducing medications and iron deficiency prevention drugs for his child.

Masoumeh Taherkhani stated that land routes cannot replace maritime trade due to logistical limitations. Turkey is currently extracting monopoly tolls from Iran. Financial routes are also being blocked, which could impose a heavy inflation wave on Iranian consumers by the end of the year.

Abbas Araghchi, Iran's foreign minister, stated in an online speech that sustainable security in the Middle East must belong to the region itself and is achieved through dialogue and cooperation. He described the military aggression by the US and Israel as illegal and unjust. He also said the war against Iran is part of a broader pattern of unpunished aggressions.
The police commander of Astaneh Ashrafiyeh announced the arrest of a citizen. The reason for the arrest was sending videos to foreign media. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Tuition fees at some private schools in Tehran have reached several hundred million tomans. Parents say that additional costs such as transportation, food, and extracurricular activities have put heavy financial pressure on families. This issue was discussed in an interview with psychoanalyst Saba Alaleh.

A citizen sent a voice message to Iran International mentioning the lack of security in schools. He said he would not send his child to school for a while. He also urged other citizens to take similar action.

Somayeh Golpour stated that less than 5% of workers in the country are members of labor organizations, and 97% have no representatives in higher labor organizations. She criticized the limited meetings of the Supreme Labor Council and the one-year extension of organizations without elections. She considered these factors as weakening the workers' ability to demand rights.

Employees of Refah store reported months of delayed salary payments and unpaid insurance premiums. Their insurance premiums have not been paid for nearly a year. They have called on the Ministry of Cooperatives, Labor, and Social Welfare and the Social Security Organization to address their situation.

Mehdi Kazemi-Qomi stated that 50 to 60 percent of the residential area in Tehran's District 11 is located in worn-out urban fabric. About 371 hectares of this district's land are in the worn-out area, ranking second after District 12. Due to its historical background and high population density, this district is prioritized in urban renewal programs.
Iranians in Australia gathered in Perth on Saturday, 28 Shahrivar. They commemorated Mahsa Amini and chanted the slogan "Regime change" in Iran. These images were published by Iran International.
The opening ceremony of the 2026 Nagoya Asian Games ended an hour ago. The Iranian delegation left their place after the parade and during the ceremony. This caused disorder in the event.
Iranians in Hobart, Australia, held a gathering to commemorate Mahsa Amini. They called for global action regarding Iran. This video was published by Iran International.

Hossein Allahkaram stated that during the funeral ceremonies of Ali Khamenei, the IRGC targeted three large ships belonging to Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the UAE. The Supreme National Security Council called these attacks unauthorized, and the naval commander was reprimanded. This incident indicates a breach of the agreement between the Islamic Republic and the United States.

The mother of Hamid Zareh explained how her son was killed by Islamic Republic agents in January 2026. She said she will seek justice for her son's blood. She emphasized that she will stand firm until the end.

The director general of education in Gilan province announced that 1544 students in the province have dropped out of school. This figure highlights existing challenges in the education sector in Gilan. Efforts to address this issue are ongoing.

Anshan Khosravi, an organizer of the Stockholm gathering on the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death, stated that they continue the path of Mahsa and other martyrs for freedom. They believe that together they will reach a free Iran. These remarks were made to an Iran International reporter.

Protesting customers of Kerman Motor gathered at the company's headquarters in Tehran. They claim the company does not deliver registered vehicles and refuses to refund payments. The protest took place in the Jannat Abad neighborhood.

The Central Committee of the Ministry of Science confirmed the expulsion of three students from Sharif University of Technology and Beheshti University related to the protests of Esfand 1404. One student was also banned from studying for five years in addition to expulsion. For the other two students, the expulsion can be changed to a three-semester suspension if they express remorse.

Ziba Aflatoun, captain of Iran's women's national basketball team in the 1974 Asian Games, spoke about the support of Empress Farah Pahlavi for women's sports, saying they encouraged and supported basketball to progress. This interview was conducted in a special program for the 2026 Asian Games.

Donald Trump, the US president, signed a bill authorizing new sanctions against Russia over the war in Ukraine. The law also extends sanctions related to Iran. This action followed congressional approval earlier this week.

Tehran's prosecutor has filed charges against the organizers of a 10-kilometer running race in Velayat Park. The race was held with men and women participating and allegedly did not comply with legal and religious regulations. The organizers claim the event was authorized by the Ministry of Interior and the Tehran Athletics Board.

Abbas Araghchi criticized military interventions in the Middle East as a cause of instability and ongoing tensions in a video message to the 2026 Global Dialogue Forum participants. He emphasized that war has become a common tool in international relations rather than a last resort. Araghchi stated that pressure and bullying never lead to peace.
A citizen stated in a video that due to rising prices, they must work 9 hours a day to buy a few groceries. This highlights the economic pressure on people. The video was sent to Iran International.

A spontaneous campaign among Iranian families has formed to boycott in-person classes. The presence of security forces and concerns about the outbreak of war are cited as reasons for the boycott. This issue was discussed in an interview with Mohsen Mohimeni.

Iran International reported the transfer of Iran's oil sales to four new trusts linked to Mohammad Javad Bavand. This issue has also been reflected in domestic media. More details are provided in an interview with Mahtab Gholizadeh.

Ali Zeinivand, spokesperson of the Ministry of Interior, stated that the 10-kilometer marathon in Tehran should not have been held simultaneously with the Janfada exercise. The Tehran prosecutor's office has filed charges against the organizers for not adhering to legal and religious regulations. The event took place on September 17, 2026, and women participated without mandatory hijab.

The expulsion and suspension rulings for Alireza Jafarzadeh from Shahid Beheshti University and Fariborz Kohanzad and Parnian Khodabakhshi from Sharif University of Technology were confirmed by the Central Disciplinary Committee of the Ministry of Science. These rulings involve three students in Tehran. The Ministry of Science has approved these rulings.

The Iranian men's handball team lost their first match on September 18th against Kuwait with a score of 26 to 24. This team was the only Iranian representative on that day. More details are provided in an interview with Alireza Modiri.

Amnesty International has published a detailed report of over 1100 pages on the crimes of the Islamic Republic in suppressing the Mahsa uprising protests. The report accuses Iranian officials of crimes against humanity. The short documentary "Iran Rising" reviews this report and the events of 2022 in Iran.

Schools reopened on September 19, but there are concerns about students' safety and rising costs. Families are avoiding sending their children to school due to war conditions and military training. Economic difficulties have also made school supplies and meals very expensive.

Iranians worldwide held protests on the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death. Matin Khaledi, an organizer in Florence, stated the aim was to honor the deceased and support prisoners awaiting execution. They also emphasized the leadership of Prince Reza Pahlavi and the national revolution.

Luqman Pourmand, a citizen from Dizaj Margur in Urmia, has been detained for over six months. His family and lawyer have no information about his whereabouts or condition. During this time, he has been denied access to his lawyer and family visits.

The US case against Halkbank was closed on June 17. Two months and 18 days later, the US Treasury sanctioned Golden Global Bank in Turkey. Mohammad Mashinchian reviews the history of sanctions from Pamukbank to Golden Global.

Mike Johnson, Speaker of the US House of Representatives, said the conflict with the Islamic Republic is not an ongoing war and is in its final stage. He emphasized the importance of keeping the Strait of Hormuz open for commercial shipping and noted that at least 25 countries can participate in this effort. Johnson called the 'Epic Wrath' operation successful and opposed limiting the US president's military powers.

Mohsen Rezaei stated that the Islamic Republic's nuclear doctrine has not changed and they remain committed to Ali Khamenei's fatwa. He outlined Tehran's conditions for ending the war as ending all fronts, releasing blocked assets, and lifting the naval blockade. Rezaei also said Tehran wants to end the conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis.

Brad Cooper, the commander of CENTCOM, stated that US forces have supported the passage of over two thousand commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz in the past two months. More than one billion barrels of crude oil have also been transported through this strait. This information was provided in his latest update.

Ata Hosseinian stated that with the reduction of oil loading from Khark and Jask and unofficial routes, Iran's official oil exports are close to zero. In the worst case, exports are estimated at about 200 to 250 thousand barrels per day. This indicates a sharp decline in the Islamic Republic's oil exports.

Bahman Ghobadi returns after five years with the horror film "The Trees Watch" at the Toronto Festival. The film stars Eva Green and is made in the horror genre. Ghobadi has registered a new experience in the horror genre with this work.

Narges Mohammadi, a human rights activist and 2023 Nobel Peace Prize laureate, stated in an interview that the Iranian people face the consequences of war, economic pressure from US sanctions, and increased internal repression. She said these conditions leave no room for breathing and that people are paying a heavy price. Mohammadi also highlighted the youth's resistance against repression.

The Pentagon is reviewing the deployment of US military forces in Europe. One of the options under consideration is the withdrawal of at least 25,000 American troops from the continent. These reviews have increased concerns among some of Washington's European allies.

Farzin Nadimi stated that the increase in security alerts in Europe is due to intensified hybrid attacks by Russia. Russia is trying to blur the line between war and peace with limited cyber and drone attacks. NATO countries are increasing drills and warnings to prevent normalization of these attacks.

Three workers in Mashhad and Langarud were injured due to lack of safety and poor working conditions. These incidents occurred because of insufficient safety measures at the workplace. More details are published by Harana News Agency.

Esmaeil Baqaei stated that traveling to New York is not attractive for Iranian diplomats but should not be missed. He emphasized that participating in the UN meeting is Iran's right and they must assert their legitimacy. Additionally, the Pakistani Interior Minister's visit to Tehran is about bilateral relations, with no special message exchange regarding mediation.

The Houthi group in Yemen claimed responsibility for two operations against sensitive targets in Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu, Saudi Arabia. They stated that attacks will continue until Saudi Arabia stops its attacks and ends the blockade of Yemen. The Houthis denied Saudi reports about targeting civilians.
A group of workers from the municipality of Kut Abdullah, Ahvaz metro project, Iran Telecommunication Factories Company, and the maintenance section of the southern railway reported wage arrears.

The senior spokesman for Iran's Armed Forces rejected the remarks by the CENTCOM commander about supporting oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, calling them 'a lie, projection, and ridiculous.من' He said these statements were a 'failed psychological operation' to boost the morale of exhausted American forces and justify the high financial and human costs. He emphasized that the initiative in the Strait of Hormoz remains with Iranُs Armed Forces.

Mehdi Mahdavi Azad said in the program "Cheshmandaz" that reports about the possible intensification of air restrictions and the halt of a significant portion of Iran's international flights have been published. The Islamic Republic has denied these reports. This issue has been raised for the coming days and weeks.

A dating app unveiled a new generation of AI agents to find suitable partners. Each user has an AI agent that finds better matches based on their characteristics. This model improves user interaction by simulating dates.

The cost of transporting goods from China to Iran has quadrupled. A queue of 3,700 trucks has formed at the Turkey border. These issues have arisen after the US naval blockade and Iran's efforts to shift trade to land routes.

Two protests were held in Tehran today. One protest was by customers of Kerman Motor and the other by victims of the Unique Finance company case. These protests were held as demonstrations of dissent.

The price of stationery in Iran has increased by 100 to 300 percent ahead of school reopening. Initial costs for a student in public schools have reached 15 million tomans. This amount does not include ongoing expenses such as school transportation and extracurricular classes.
Niusha Saremi warned about the possibility of Putin attacking NATO territory. Preparations have increased from Switzerland to Poland. This topic was discussed in the audio version of Titrawol.

Amir Gorosi, a 60-year-old political prisoner, was sentenced to 10 years in prison by Branch 29 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. He was accused of sending images and videos to foreign media. He is currently held in Tehran Grand Prison.
A citizen in Pardis County was arrested by the Intelligence Forces of the IRGC for producing and sending a video to a foreign-based television network.

CENTCOM announced that over the past five months, coinciding with the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic's ports, more than one billion barrels of crude oil from Persian Gulf countries have passed through the Strait of Hormuz with the support of American forces.

Hakan Fidan, Turkey's foreign minister, stated that Saudi Arabia does not wish to enter the war between the US and the Islamic Republic. He said Turkey is ready to respond to Saudi Arabia's military needs within the framework of the Makkah defense coalition. Fidan also described the Makkah coalition as an influential mechanism.

Alan Bastakian said the Cyrus the Great event provides an opportunity to introduce transition programs to politicians. He noted the presence of Canadian politicians as a sign of increased attention to Iran's future. Prince Reza Pahlavi was also recognized as the future leader of Iran.

Barcelona has reached an agreement with Raphinha to extend his contract until 2030. Contracts for Xavi Spart and Marc Bernal will also be renewed. Raphinha has performed excellently this season and wishes to finish his playing career at Barcelona.

Salar Gholami, former captain of Iran's national boxing team, stated that Reza Pahlavi's position is clear to the Iranian people. He expects Canadian and other governments to recognize this position. The presence of representatives from Canada's Liberal and Conservative parties at the Cyrus the Great event highlights the importance of Reza Pahlavi's leadership issue.

Babak Amini stated at the second Cyrus the Great event in Toronto that the event can bring hope to the people of Iran. He added that artists have a responsibility to strengthen unity and solidarity. The greater the convergence, the more impactful it will be.

Mohsen Rezaei stated that the Islamic Republic is in contact with a Qatari mediator who has conveyed Tehran's conditions for ending the war to Washington. The conditions include ending the war on all fronts, releasing blocked Iranian assets, and ending the naval blockade. The Islamic Republic is awaiting Trump's response to these conditions.

The second edition of the 'Cyrus the Great' event focusing on Iran's historical heritage and the country's future is being held in Toronto. More than three thousand people are attending the event. Prince Reza Pahlavi will speak in the final part of the gathering.
The US plans to initiate an air blockade of Iran following a naval blockade. This topic was discussed in the audio version of Cheshmandaz. More details are provided in this report.

Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, announced that Iran has communicated seven conditions to the US for starting any negotiation. The conditions include ending the war, releasing blocked Iranian assets, and ending the naval blockade. Communication between Tehran and Washington continues through Qatari and Pakistani mediators.

The schedule of Iranian athletes for the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya on Sunday, 29 Shahrivar, has been announced. Iranian representatives' competitions start at 3 AM Tehran time. It will be a busy day for the Iranian sports delegation.

Pierre Poilievre, leader of Canada's Conservative Party, called the Islamic Republic a "tyrannical terrorist" that has taken freedom from the Iranian people. He said the Islamic Republic will be overthrown and the Iranian people will achieve freedom. He also expressed hope that Prince Reza Pahlavi will return to Iran and raise the Lion and Sun flag.

Forough Kenani stated that holding events like 'Cyrus the Great' shows Western politicians that there are political and economic capacities for the post-Islamic Republic era. These conferences reduce concerns about Iran's future after regime change and introduce Iranian capabilities. The continuation of these events also sends a message of hope and solidarity to Iranians inside the country.

Pierre Poilievre stated that the Islamic Republic does not represent the Iranian people and Canada should have no diplomatic relations with it. He called for increased sanctions and the expulsion of IRGC members from Canada. He also emphasized pursuing justice for the victims of flight PS-752.

Last week, a creditor's lawyer and an enforcement officer visited Persepolis club to seize assets, but the specified assets were not found and the seizure was not executed. Two days ago, a court ordered the seizure and auction of the club's assets, resulting in the sale of 288 items of equipment. The buyer was a company affiliated with one of the club's main shareholder banks.

Prince Reza Pahlavi stated in his speech in Toronto that the Dey epic was not a fleeting excitement and that the Islamic Republic committed a major crime at that time. He emphasized their goal is to overthrow the Islamic Republic and achieve a free and prosperous Iran. Their four key principles include preserving Iran's territorial integrity, separation of religion from government, individual freedoms and equality of citizens, and the nation's right to determine its future through free and fair elections.

Reza Pahlavi stated in his speech in Toronto that there is a split and distrust at the highest decision-making levels of the Islamic Republic. He said Mojtaba is missing and if alive, he does not dare to make any sound in a dark basement. He also mentioned that many regime forces have declared separation through secure communication channels.

Reza Pahlavi emphasized the dignity and authenticity of the Iranian nation in his speech in Toronto and said the dawn of Iran's freedom is near. He added that the people are more determined and organized than ever to overthrow the Islamic Republic. He also referred to the people's resistance against the regime's attempts to buy their will.

Reza Pahlavi stated at the 'Cyrus the Great' event in Toronto that the main burden of the fight for freedom lies with the Iranian people and that the 'Lion and Sun' revolution has deep roots in society. He described the events of January 2026 as the result of a long path of protests from 2016 to 2022. He also accused the Islamic Republic of committing crimes during the January 2023 protests and said the opposition is now more experienced and united.

Reza Pahlavi stated at the 'Cyrus the Great' event that the tactics of opponents of the Islamic Republic have changed, but the goal remains to overthrow the regime. He rejected two lies by the Islamic Republic about the opposition's despair and emphasized four common principles among the opponents. He also said that millions of Iranians inside and outside the country are coordinated and organized.

Reza Pahlavi announced in his speech in Toronto that his team has made tactical changes in their strategy due to new conditions and killings by the Islamic Republic. He emphasized that the goal remains unchanged: overthrowing the Islamic Republic and achieving a free and prosperous Iran. He also warned that the Islamic Republic is trying to spread despair.

Reza Pahlavi stated at the 'Cyrus the Great' event in Toronto that the greatest enemy of Iran is the Islamic Republic. He emphasized cooperation with other countries to free Iran based on national interests, territorial integrity, and national sovereignty. He also described the overthrow of the Islamic Republic as a multi-stage process requiring patience, continuity, and planning.

Ivar Farhadi described the four principles proposed by Prince Reza Pahlavi as the basis for cooperation among opponents of the Islamic Republic. He emphasized that those who do not accept these principles cannot play a positive role in overthrowing the regime. He also stressed the need for organization, unity among opponents, and cooperation based on Iran's national interests.

Melissa Lantsman, a Conservative Party representative from Canada, said at the Cyrus the Great event in Toronto that opponents of the Islamic Republic will one day gather in a free Iran. She emphasized that while the regime has tools of repression, the Iranian people have a power beyond that. Lantsman also expressed the Conservative Party of Canada's support for Iranians fighting for freedom.

The US State Department, citing the risk of rapid escalation of tensions and the ongoing conflict between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, urged its citizens in nine Middle Eastern countries to exercise increased vigilance. It also warned of possible flight cancellations, airspace closures, and other travel disruptions. The security alert covers Iraq, Bahrain, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Iran, Qatar, Lebanon, Kuwait, and Jordan.

Donald Trump returned early from Camp David to the White House on the evening of Saturday, 29 Shahrivar. The reason for his early return has not been announced. This occurred ahead of his trip to New York to attend the United Nations General Assembly.

The Tehran Seminary management has called on the judiciary to take action against the organizers of the marathon in Velayat Park where some women participated without mandatory hijab. The institution considers this issue a religious and social duty and opposes normalizing violations. The seminary emphasized it will not allow the erosion of the sanctity of laws in society.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, stated that two images of Iran exist: the criminal Islamic Republic and a generation striving to overthrow it and build a free Iran. This generation has returned to its identity roots and sees Cyrus as a symbol of identity. They also refer to Prince Reza Pahlavi as "Cyrus."

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, described Cyrus as the national identity anchor and a pillar of the National Revolution discourse. He said the revolution started in November 2016 and continued through subsequent uprisings. He characterized the current generation as returning to their identity roots and calling Reza Pahlavi by the name Cyrus.

Kayhan newspaper stated that Iran is not in an economic crisis nor close to one. It warned that enemies still aim to harm Iran economically. Kayhan urged officials not to hide facts but also not to portray Iran as weak.

Takumi Hojo from Japan won the men's individual triathlon in Gamagori with a time of 52 minutes and 56 seconds, earning the first gold medal of the games. Zhang Zirui from China took silver, and Arlan Zhanbayev from Kazakhstan won bronze. This medal is the first of 469 gold medals to be awarded in this two-week tournament.

A group of Iranians living in Norway gathered in Oslo on September 19. The gathering was held to commemorate the fourth anniversary of the Mahsa uprising. They also expressed support for Prince Reza Pahlavi.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said in a parliamentary webinar that the resistance of the Iranian people guarantees the country's security and can create opportunities for economic and strategic openings. He emphasized that the dichotomy of war or negotiation is not real and both must be pursued. Ghalibaf added that the steadfastness of the people will elevate Iran to a new level of power and prosperity.

Fatemeh Sadeghi lost the bronze medal match in the women's individual kata karate event at the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya against China-Hui Shuan from Taiwan. The match ended with a score of four to one in favor of her opponent. With this defeat, Iran lost its first medal.

Najmeh Amini, a 23-year-old student, was arrested during the national revolution in Mashhad and sentenced to death. She has been denied the right to choose a lawyer and fair trial, and pressured for forced confession during interrogation. Najmeh Amini called on people to be her voice in a phone call from Vakilabad prison.

The mayor of Moscow announced that Russian defense forces have destroyed over 1,600 Ukrainian drones since Saturday. 450 drones were targeted near Moscow. He described the attack as unprecedented and said its aim was to disrupt the elections.

Sadegh Beigdeli stated that the Makkah Pact is facing its first serious test, and it remains to be seen how much Pakistan and Turkey will support Saudi Arabia. He added that the Islamic Republic is using Bab al-Mandab as one of its last geopolitical cards. Although using these cards has provided temporary advantages, strategically it has ultimately worked against the Islamic Republic.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated in a parliamentary webinar that the path of one-sided imposition by the enemy is closed and Iran's diplomatic positions are clear and non-negotiable. He emphasized that until the Islamic Republic's conditions and American commitments are fulfilled, there will be no return to previous negotiation conditions. Ghalibaf also said the old American order in West Asia has collapsed and Islamic countries should establish a new order.

The police supervising public places in western Tehran province announced the closure of four cafes in Shahriar county. This action was part of a monitoring plan aimed at addressing social irregularities. The news was reported by Harana News Agency.

A group of Iranians living in the UK gathered in the streets of London on Saturday, 28 Shahrivar, to commemorate the fourth anniversary of the Woman, Life, Freedom uprising. This event was reported through videos received by Iran International.

Hossein Ali Haji Deligani, representative of Shahin Shahr, called for Iran to leave the NPT. He stated that remaining in the NPT harms the country. A group of representatives have submitted an urgent bill to exit the NPT.

A group of Iranians residing in the USA and Australia gathered on Saturday, September 19, to commemorate the anniversary of Mahsa Amini's uprising in San Jose and Adelaide. This gathering was reported based on videos received by Iran International.

Kambiz Tavana mentioned Donald Trump's early return from Camp David. The US State Department has issued warnings to its citizens in nine Middle Eastern countries. These developments occurred after the Houthis fired a ballistic missile towards Riyadh.

Ebrahim Azizi announced that the unveiling of the agreement on the Strait of Hormuz, which was to take place in Muscat, has been postponed. He emphasized that the Islamic Republic will not allow the return of Americans to the Persian Gulf and that negotiating again with the US is meaningless. He also stated that if membership in the NPT no longer serves Iran's interests, Tehran will take appropriate action.

The match between Lyon and Rennes in the fifth week of Ligue 1 was stopped for 15 minutes due to an offensive banner by Lyon fans against Saint-Étienne. The referee stopped the game at the 36th minute, and players left the field at the 40th minute. After the issue was resolved, the match resumed.

The Alborz Court of Appeals confirmed the 18-year prison sentence for Manouchehr Bakhtiari. The sentence no longer includes 74 lashes. Bakhtiari was convicted of various charges including forming a group against national security.

Ukraine carried out a large-scale drone attack on Moscow on Sunday, 29 Shahrivar. The mayor of Moscow called it the largest drone attack on the Russian capital so far. Released images show fire and smoke at the Moscow oil refinery, which supplies about 40% of Moscow's fuel market.

A group of Iranians living in Germany took to the streets on Saturday, September 19, to commemorate the anniversary of Mahsa's uprising. The gatherings took place in Nuremberg, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, Hamburg, and Düsseldorf. This information is based on videos received by Iran International.

Kamran Ghazanfari, a Tehran representative, stated that the impeachment plan of the president has been proposed due to economic, political, and cultural conditions. He said this issue is within the powers of the parliament members and carrying it out is part of their duties. He also emphasized that the Speaker blocking this plan would be illegal.

The head of the Hemophilia Association in Kermanshah province reported that increased prices and shortages of drugs have disrupted the treatment of hemophilia patients. Last year, about 26 hemophilia patients died due to lack of access to their medications. He emphasized the need for sustainable support from the country's insurance and health system for these patients.

The family of the missing person Mohsen Rashidi Khani Abadi distributed stationery packages in his memory ahead of the new school year. This action was shared on social media. The distribution took place to mark the beginning of the school year.

Mohsen Rezaei stated that if neighboring countries cooperate with the US in sanctions and economic blockade against Iran, they will be punished. He threatened to target their ships in the Strait of Hormuz and possibly restrict their passage. Additionally, American companies in the region and US ships in the Indian Ocean will be targeted.

A recreational and sports event was held at Araz Hotel in Nowshahr with women present without mandatory hijab. This led to intervention by security and judicial authorities. The Nowshahr prosecutor's office announced it will deal with illegal cases.

Najmeh Amini, one of the detainees of the December 2025 protests, announced that her death sentence has been issued by the judiciary. This news was shared in an audio message from Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. Her death sentence was issued on September 15.

Mohsen Rezaei stated that Tehran's conditions for stopping the war have been conveyed to the US via Qatar. The Islamic Republic is trying to persuade Washington to return to negotiations amid naval blockade and sanctions pressure. Simultaneously, two paths of diplomacy and escalating tensions are being pursued.

A group of Iranians living in Sweden marched in Gothenburg on Saturday, 28 Shahrivar. The march was held to commemorate the anniversary of Mahsa's uprising. Videos of the event were sent to Iran International.

Elham Kholas Ardestani, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Isfahan, was released from Dolatabad prison in Isfahan on Saturday, 28 Shahrivar, after posting a bail of two billion tomans. This news was reported by the HRANA news agency. Her release occurred following the payment of bail.

The Islamic Republic is pressuring its proxy forces in Yemen to maintain the blockade of the Bab al-Mandab Strait. The goal is to raise global oil prices and politically harm Donald Trump and the Republicans. This report was published by Israel Hayom.
